Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who is, or who
by reason of a mistake of fact and not by reason of a mistake of law in good
faith believes himself to be, bound by law to do it.

and, after due enquiry, believing Z to be Y, arrests Z. A has committed no
offence.

original.text: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed, intentionally omits to give any information respecting that offence which he is legally bound to give, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both. Giving false information respecting an offence committed.

phase11.final_answer: Section 14 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita states that no act is considered an offence if performed by a person who, due to a mistake of fact and not a mistake of law, believes in good faith that they are bound by law to perform that act.
phase11.summary_answer: Section 14 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita states that no act is considered an offence if performed by a person who, due to a mistake of fact and not a mistake of law, believes in good faith that they are bound by law to perform that act.
phase11.detailed_answer: Section 14 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, provides that nothing is an offence if done by a person who believes, in good faith and due to a mistake of fact (not law), that they are legally bound to act. For example, a soldier acting under orders or a court officer mistakenly arresting the wrong person under a court order would not be committing an offence. This section emphasizes the importance of the individual's belief and the nature of the mistake involved.
